[tense] “I’m sure a teacher with such good recommendations as yourself will know better than to start wandering about on a new School. As you know, Schools are no place for the faint of heart. Until you become familiar with our most dangerous regions and get acquainted with the main predators of our local fauna, please stick to my directions and you’ll have no trouble getting to your destination. Now I must excuse myself, as I have a parents meeting today. I’ll check on you by lunchtime, all right? Good luck with the class”.
Feeling somewhat dazed by her unending stream of words, but also quite elated at the success of my infiltration attempt, I decided to…

find my students on 5B and give them a masterclass...

look for the teachers room…

spy on Miss Summer’s parent meeting…

find my students on 5B and give them a masterclass on ostrich reproduction. I’ve always believed that if someone had just done that for me when I was their age, they would have saved me from becoming the mental shipwreck I currently am. Unfortunately, class 5B wasn’t as easy to find as it seemed, and by the time I managed to reach it the class had already ended and children were running towards their freedom. I followed them to the main entrance and went home with a bitter feeling of disappointment at having wasted my one true chance in life at sacrificing myself for the greater good.

ran away from him, afraid he would give me away to a teacher. In the end, though, I ended up getting so lost I wasn’t sure I would be able to get out of the school even if I wanted, so by the time I heard the lunch time bell and found a window that connecting to the outside, I gave a silent prayer of gratitude and escaped through through it, swearing never to set a foot on that accursed place again.

I won’t describe in detail the trials and tribulations we went through on our grand journey. Suffice it to say that eventually we made our way to the teacher’s room - although my guide lost one finger on the way, during a fight with a particularly ferocious tribe of class skippers that were competing with us for vital resources. In the teacher’s room we burned the concierge’s purse, as promised, thus sealing our pledge of eternal goodwill before parting ways. It wasn’t until I had almost given up my search for clues that I found something truly valuable: a copy of the school keys for the main gate, hidden away in a small locker of the teacher’s room. I pocketed them and quickly made my exit to the outside, to prepare for my return.

... spy on my neighbour. She lives two floors up. I went out in my sleepers and...

... Knocked on her door...

... Peeked through the keyhole...

... peeked through the keyhole.

It was just dark.

I saw my neighbour. She was writing a note on a piece of paper.

There was a long rope coiled on the ground and some red cylinders with a string sticking out of them next to it.

She was writing a note on a piece of paper.

I saw my neighbour on the ground with a red face fighting to breathe. The street sweeper was holding a phone in one hand and the bouquet of flowers in the other. Poor guy.

... a really old lady sitting on a bench, so peacefully. I went to sit next to her, and she seemed startled for a second until she squeezed her eyes and said, “Timothy? Is that you, dear?”

“Err, I... no.”

“Certainly.”

“Su... Roses,” I replied shrewdly. I wasn’t so dumb to reveal my true allegiances to a complete stranger just like that. What if he was the sunflower murderer?
“Ah”, he said, looking somehow disappointed with my answer. “Well, I do have some roses, if you want them”. 
Seedless flowers hold no appeal to me, but I took the roses anyway, not wanting to give myself away.
I was getting more and more uncomfortable with my charade, as if I had betrayed my pure devotion of sunflowers, so I thanked the gardener and walked away soon after that.

“Cheer up, it will only last a few hours”, I said, trying to help. I wasn’t sure he was actually on my side, but he was nice to his flowers. 
“Yes”, he said absentmindedly. “Yes, I suppose you’re right”. 
After that he just sat there, waiting, and a while later I decided to leave.

I took the sandwich. What can I say? I was hungry, and it was a really good looking sandwich.

Leave him alone. We all need our privacy from time to time. Perhaps later would be a better time.
